YOUR SECTOR • Mirror Market

Meet Mirror Market

Know the themes. Meet the people. Explore several everyday situations.

Online identity, digital footprints and privacy

Try a profile audit, change the audience and build a public bio. Share the version of you that you choose.

Online identity

The picture of you that your profile, posts and interactions create. It can be selective and still honest.

Digital footprint

The traces left by online activity, including copies and posts made by other people.

Audience and consent

Who can see this? Has each person agreed to this use? A private account reduces the audience but cannot guarantee secrecy.

Seren

Proud of her team and her artwork. Wants a profile that feels like her.

Mina

Likes celebrating with friends, but wants a say in which photos become public.

By the end, you will be able to:
  • Notice revealing details
  • Choose a suitable audience
  • Share achievements thoughtfully

Use the fictional details given. You never need to share a personal incident.

AUDIENCE LAB

The same team photograph

Compare two settings. Who gains or loses access?

What might remain outside Seren’s control, even after deleting?

A footprint includes what other people save or post. Settings are useful controls, not an undo button for everything.

Ripple City field guide

Key terms

Online identityThe picture of you that your profile, posts and interactions create. It can be selective and still honest.
Digital footprintThe traces left by online activity, including copies and posts made by other people.
Audience and consentWho can see this? Has each person agreed to this use? A private account reduces the audience but cannot guarantee secrecy.
Digital identityThe picture of a person created by profiles, posts, actions and other people.
AudienceThe people who can see, receive or later discover content.
Context collapseWhen different audiences meet content intended for only one group.
AuthenticGenuine and truthful, while still choosing suitable boundaries.
PrivacyControl over who can access information and how it is used.
